body:
It seamed to be there before but can you explain why we set the page to `page - 1` when there's a UI state for page? Do we considerer `page: 1` to be the first page (i.e. `0` in code)?

If so, it's worth adding a comment.
We don't care about it being the same reference. We only want to check the value, right?
Can we not use a snapshot for this? That's small enough to use `toEqual` and it creates less context switch.
Same comment regarding the value instead of the reference.
At some point IIRC it was important. But anyway my PR move this code but didn't change it at all. Only the code related to `getWidgetSearchParameters` changes (implem + tests).

Yes it is. At the API/`SearchParameters` level page is indexed on 0. Inside the `uiState` it's indexed on 1. Most of the time users expect the first page to be `1` not `0`, especially inside their URL. That's why we have this (see the [`getWidgetState`](https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch.js/blob/299ffe28006deb516bdc969da8089e703623be6b/src/connectors/pagination/connectPagination.js#L158-L165)).
It's still an opportunity to improve this, that's a quick win and a small effort both for you and the reviewers.
